customComposites.semanticRole: Graph-anchored explanation and persistent trace for fields that were mapped automatically while creating a connection.
customComposites.affordance: A named PrimeVue reveal button at the affected edge opens the field mapping explanation; settled traces retain named PrimeVue dismiss controls.

rejectedPrimeVueCompositions.reason: PrimeVue Popover requires a DOM trigger target, while this surface follows a virtual VueFlow edge midpoint through pan, zoom, and collision-aware placement.
A global notification would detach the explanation from the affected edge and cannot preserve the source-to-target field geometry.

primeVueVisualSibling.usage: PrimeVue Button owns activation, focus, severity, radius, border, surface, and dismiss-control visuals inside the graph-positioned composite.

inheritedRuntimeProperties: PrimeVue Button keyboard activation and theme focus treatment
PrimeVue severity, disabled, border, surface, radius, and typography tokens
invariantProperties: Placement remains anchored to the current rendered edge midpoint.
Each explanation retains its source and target field names.
Opening and dismissing are exposed through named PrimeVue buttons.
The composite introduces no raw control or local button appearance system.
customComposites.novelGeometry: The composite is projected from VueFlow graph coordinates and must track a virtual edge midpoint; no PrimeVue overlay composition owns that geometry.

accessibilityEvidence.assertion: The reveal and settled-trace actions render as enabled, named native buttons through PrimeVue and emit their public actions.
The retained reveal surface is a PrimeVue button and has no manual role, tabindex, or keydown activation contract.

visualEvidence.scenario: Reveal and settled-trace variants render mapping pairs and their PrimeVue-managed controls.

customComposites.semanticRole: Nonmodal graph-anchored editor for resolving an ambiguous connection intent before the workflow graph is mutated.
customComposites.affordance: A named nonmodal region appears beside the proposed edge, focuses its PrimeVue input, previews validation state, and provides named PrimeVue accept and cancel actions.

rejectedPrimeVueCompositions.reason: PrimeVue Popover requires a DOM trigger target, while the editor is positioned from a virtual connection midpoint and collision-adjusted canvas coordinates.
A modal dialog would trap focus, obscure the canvas, and remove the spatial context needed to understand which proposed connection is being resolved.

primeVueVisualSibling.usage: The composite follows PrimeVue Popover surface semantics while PrimeVue InputText, Button, and Message own all interactive and status presentation.

inheritedRuntimeProperties: PrimeVue InputText focus, invalid, disabled, and theme behavior
PrimeVue Button keyboard activation, loading, disabled, severity, and theme behavior
PrimeVue Message validation and status presentation
invariantProperties: Placement remains anchored to the proposed connection midpoint.
The named nonmodal region focuses the intent input on entry.
Escape cancels the proposal without mutating the graph.
Only an accepted valid intent creates the connection.
Superseded validation requests cannot overwrite current state.
customComposites.novelGeometry: The composite follows an uncommitted VueFlow connection represented only by graph coordinates; it has no stable DOM target for a library overlay anchor.

accessibilityEvidence.assertion: The editor exposes a named nonmodal region, focuses the input on entry, supports Escape cancellation, and preserves named accept and cancel actions.
Collision-aware placement preserves the graph-coordinate relationship at viewport boundaries.

visualEvidence.scenario: Editing, validation, acceptance, and cancellation states render with PrimeVue-managed controls and messages.
